paras: It was a holiday. The local market was full of people. The toy shop opened at 9 a.m. There were many toys in the shop, such as wooden toys, soft toys, board games, bats, balls and many others. All the toys in the toy shop were waiting excitedly to see who would buy them.
“Look there!” shouted the toy kitten. The toys saw two girls coming towards the shop. But the girls passed by, only looking at the toys through the windows.
“Oh, no!” exclaimed all the toys at once.

After some time, a girl and a little boy stopped at the door of the toy shop. Their father stopped too. The girl pointed at the board games displayed in the shop. Finally, she chose the game Snakes and Ladders.
“Ohhhh!” sighed the toys together.
Next, a woman and her son came into the shop. The toys were excited to see them. A talking doll said, “It would be so nice if they picked me up!”
“I would be happy if they chose me,” thought the toy elephant.
“Namaste! How may I help you?” asked the toy shopkeeper.
“Namaste! I want to buy a toy for my son,” said the woman, looking at the toys on the racks.
“Aayi! I want that Vande Bharat train!” said the little boy, pointing at the toy train.
What do you call your mother?
Aayi bought the Vande Bharat toy train. The little boy was very happy.
Then two girls came into the shop. The toys looked at them eagerly.
“Zooooooooooooom! Friends! I think they would like to fly me,” said the aeroplane confidently.
“Trin ... Trin ...! I think they may like to play with me,” thought the toy phone.
One girl bought marbles, and the other bought the toy aeroplane.
After a while, a group of children came into the toy shop.
“Wow! I like this toy elephant,” said the girl with long hair.
“I will take this spinning top,” said the boy with the red cap.
“I like these cute dancing dolls,” said the boy in the blue shirt.
The children bought the toys they liked and left the shop cheerfully. All the toys were happy because they had found loving homes and children to play with them.
Section A: Describing Words
Describing words tell us more about naming words. For example, red tells us about a colour, talking tells us what someone or something does, and blue tells us about a colour.

sections.heading: A1. Add a suitable word from the help box to each naming word. You may use the same word more than once.

items.a: white (cotton, yellow, brown or clean also work)

sections.heading: A2. Underline the describing word in each sentence.

items.q: The little boy has a red ball.
The elephant has a long trunk.

paras: Section B: Plurals – Adding ‘s’
We add -s to many naming words to show that there is more than one. These words are called plural words.
Examples: toy – toys; boy – boys.

sections.heading: B1. Write the plural of each word by adding ‘s’.
B2. Choose the correct word to complete each sentence.

items.q: The children play with their (toy / toys).
There are three (cup / cups) on the table.
We can see two (bird / birds) in the tree.

paras: Section C: Plurals – Adding ‘es’
For some naming words, we add -es to make the plural.
Examples: box – boxes; class – classes.

sections.heading: C1. Write the plural of each word by adding ‘es’.
sections.note: One has been done for you: box – boxes.

sections.heading: C2. Fill in the blanks with the correct plural form of the word in brackets.

items.q: There are two ______ outside the school. (bus)
I have four ______ in my school bag. (brush)
The shopkeeper packed the sweets in small ______. (pouch)
